summary: the file is not JSON or CSV the readers can follow, or its top level is not an object, so no payment was read
fix: Write the batch as one JSON object or as a CSV table with a header row (docs/inputs.md), and fix the line named.

summary: a field the checks need is not in the batch: the payments, a payment id, a beneficiary country, a rail, an amount, the currency and account of a bank payment, or the network, token and wallet of a stablecoin payment
fix: Add the field named; docs/inputs.md lists what each payment needs.

summary: a key or column the tool does not read, often a misspelt one; its value was left out of every check
fix: Correct the spelling to a field of docs/inputs.md, or remove it.

summary: a value of the wrong type or form: an object where text belongs, a rail the tool does not know, a field the rail of the payment does not take, a rate that is not a decimal above 0, or a batch field that differs from row to row
fix: Write the value as docs/inputs.md shows: text for names, codes, accounts and addresses, decimal numbers for amounts and rates.

summary: a column is named twice in the header of a CSV file, so two readers of the file could take different values; the second column was left out
fix: Keep one column of each name. In a JSON file a key written twice stops the reader (batch-unreadable).

summary: the batch holds a private key, a seed or a mnemonic, under a key or column named for one or as a value shaped like one; the tool never reads it and never shows it
fix: Remove the value from the file and from wherever the file was copied, treat it as exposed and move the funds it controls. A payout batch names wallets by their public address only.

summary: an IBAN that fails the MOD 97-10 check of ISO 13616, or is not in the form of an IBAN at all (two letters, two check digits, up to 30 letters and digits)
fix: Copy the IBAN again from the beneficiary, in electronic form or in groups of four; never correct the check digits by hand to make it pass.

summary: an IBAN whose length is not the one the IBAN registry of Swift gives its country; the IBAN of a country out of the saved registry is checked for its check digits only
fix: Copy the IBAN again from the beneficiary; an IBAN of the right country always has the length of the registry.

summary: the country of the IBAN is not the beneficiary country, and not a territory the registry lists under that IBAN prefix
fix: Check the beneficiary country and the IBAN with the beneficiary; when the account is abroad on purpose, keep the warning and say so in the review.
own: comparing the country of the IBAN with the beneficiary country is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a beneficiary may hold an account abroad, and the registry only says which territories a prefix covers

summary: a BIC that is not 8 or 11 characters of the form of ISO 9362 (four letters or digits, two letters of a country, two letters or digits, an optional branch code of three), or whose country letters are not a country code
fix: Copy the BIC again from the bank of the beneficiary, in capitals and with no spaces.

summary: the country letters of the BIC are not the beneficiary country, or a territory the IBAN registry lists under that country
fix: Check the BIC with the beneficiary; when the bank is abroad on purpose, keep the warning and say so in the review.
own: comparing the country of the BIC with the beneficiary country is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the BIC page gives the place of the country code, not a rule that the bank and the beneficiary share a country

summary: a currency, a source currency or a debit currency that is not an alphabetic code of the ISO 4217 list SIX keeps, written in capitals
fix: Write the three capital letters of the currency as list one of ISO 4217 gives them, such as EUR, USD or JPY.

summary: an amount of a bank payment with more decimal places than the minor unit ISO 4217 gives its currency, such as JPY with any fraction or EUR with three places
fix: Round the amount to the minor unit of the currency before the batch is sent, and make sure the rounding is the one the beneficiary is owed.

summary: an amount that is 0, negative or not a plain decimal number (a sign, an exponent, a currency sign or a thousands separator)
fix: Write the amount as a plain decimal number above 0, such as 1500.00, and move reversals and fees to a file of their own.
own: refusing an amount of 0, a negative amount and an amount in another notation is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; none of the cited pages sets a rule on how a batch writes an amount

summary: an amount above the limit --max-amount sets for every payment or for its currency or token; the check runs only when the option is given
fix: Check the payment with its approver before the batch is sent, or set the limit your team has agreed with --max-amount.
own: a limit on the amount of one payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the limit is the team's own, and the tool has none of its own

summary: a beneficiary country that is not a two-letter code of ISO 3166-1 as the UN M49 table lists them, written in capitals, such as UK for GB
fix: Write the two capital letters of the country, such as GB for the United Kingdom.

summary: two payments share a payment id (compared without case and outer spaces), so the second is refused or, where the id is not checked, paid as well
fix: Give every payment an id of its own and keep it the same when the batch is sent again, so that a provider can refuse a payment it has already made.
own: asking for an id of its own for each payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; providers use the id to find a payment and to refuse one sent twice, and no cited page sets the rule

summary: two payments go to the same account (IBAN, account number and BIC, or wallet on a network) for the same amount in the same currency or token
fix: Check that the two payments are meant; remove one when the same payment was written twice.
own: looking for two payments of one amount to one account is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; two such payments can be right, such as two invoices of the same amount

summary: a payment with no beneficiary name, which cannot be screened against sanctions lists or matched to the account holder
fix: Give the full name of the beneficiary as the bank or the wallet provider knows it.
own: asking for a name on every payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the name is what sanctions screening and the bank of the beneficiary read, and the cited pages are about codes and accounts

summary: a beneficiary name with fewer than three letters or digits, too short to screen or to match
fix: Write the full name of the beneficiary, not initials or a placeholder.
own: the least length of a name is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; three letters is the tool's own floor, and a real name can be that short

summary: the total the batch gives for a currency or token is not the sum of its payments in that unit, or a unit with payments has no total
fix: Work out the totals again from the rows, and find the row that was added or lost before the batch is sent.
own: comparing the totals of a batch with its rows is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a control total is how many banks and providers catch a changed file, and no cited page sets the rule

summary: a wallet address not in the form of its network: 0x and 40 hex digits (not the zero address) on an EVM network, 32 to 44 base58 characters on Solana, T and 33 base58 characters on Tron
fix: Copy the wallet address again from the beneficiary, and confirm it with a small test payment before a large one.

summary: a stablecoin payment in a token that is not in the list of tokens the batch may pay in (USDC and USDT unless --tokens sets another)
fix: Pay in a token of the list, or give the tokens your team pays in with --tokens.
own: a list of tokens a batch may pay in is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; the default list is the tool's own and --tokens sets yours

summary: a stablecoin payment on a network out of the tool's table, or in a token the table does not list on that network
fix: Check by hand that the issuer of the token lists a contract on the network, and how a wallet address on it is written.
own: the table of networks and of the tokens on each is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; no cited page gives one, and a pair out of it is a question, not an error

summary: a bank payment in a currency other than its source currency, or the debit currency of the batch, with no FX rate
fix: Give the rate the batch was priced at in fxRate, so that the amount debited is known before the batch is sent.
own: asking for the rate of a converted payment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the pages it cites; a bank can convert at its own rate, and the batch then debits an amount no one checked
